BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter
Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of
Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)
Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims
is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same
caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.
Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public
registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the
Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or
public records.
Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller
will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the
counterparty's written consent.
Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding)
will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.
Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing
bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds
flow.)
Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio
matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.
Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter
and is not expected to be material.
Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course
operating costs.
Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime
above.
Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and
records are fictional.
1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including
DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.
2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause
11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final
written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.
3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security
is included.
4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of
every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of
non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject
to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft
Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or
on-costs apply.

timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised
person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation
remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no
loss amount.
7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as
a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.
8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each
(AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether
each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale
consent is required merely because shares are sold.
10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of
the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the
Buyer has completed its own verification.
11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer
must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged / internal. The Seller's materials are the counterparty's draft and have been reviewed against our playbook only. Nothing in them has been treated as agreed, cleared or authoritative.

## 1. Threshold observation – characterisations vs. facts

The Seller's cover note repeatedly uses conclusory language ("agreed price mechanics", "addressed", "considered adequate", "settled", "not expected to be material", "fair and balanced"). None of these has been confirmed through our authority process, and several are contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter, which is notably more candid than the cover note (e.g. Bluefen is "addressed" in the note but the Disclosure Letter confirms no consent exists; Riverlark is "addressed" but is unpaid with no discharge). We should rely on the factual admissions in the Disclosure Letter and reject the characterisations in the cover note. Nothing in the Seller package should be described internally as "agreed".

## 2. Departures from the playbook – issue by issue

### 2.1 General warranty cap (cl 12.1) – REJECT
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- Playbook: 25% / AUD 6,000,000 opening; 20% is a fallback usable **only** with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. **No such authority has been given.**
- The fact that the Seller's number happens to match our fallback does not clear it. We respond at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. If the team wishes to move, that is a decision for Amelia Frost in writing, referencing this specific Seller draft, before we signal anything.

### 2.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2) – REJECT, substantial gap
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
- Playbook: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
- The Seller is 5x our position on both numbers and has switched to a deductible structure. Combined with the knowledge bar and general disclosure (below), this would hollow out the warranty package. Push back on all three elements; the tipping (first-dollar) structure is the most important of the three.

### 2.3 Claims period (cl 12.3/13) – REJECT
- Seller: 18 months.
- Playbook: 24 months; 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval (none given). Respond at 24 months.
- Separately, the Seller's proposal that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" is a hidden general-regime override. It would sweep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims, and specific indemnities, into the general caps/time bars by default. Playbook requires these categories to be kept separate. Delete and replace with a clause stating that the general limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims and do not apply to any other category unless expressly stated.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title claims – REJECT outright
- Seller: title and capacity warranties subject to the same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- Playbook: separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap recovery for not actually acquiring the shares. This is a core deal-protection point; no flexibility.

### 2.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) – REJECT
- Playbook: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one may waive this.
- The Seller draft contains **no fraud carve-out at all**. This is non-negotiable and must be inserted expressly. The same clauses also need to be confined so that specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses if indemnified), Title and Tax are not caught.

### 2.6 Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2) – REJECT general disclosure
- Seller: deemed disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- Playbook: specific, fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Delete paras 1.1 and 1.2. Require that only matters fairly disclosed in the specific disclosures (paras 2–10), with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter, qualify the Warranties. Para 1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable as a standard reservation, but it cannot be used to argue that a disclosed fact is not a disclosed fact.

### 2.7 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) – DELETE
- Seller: no claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
- This is a blanket, constructive-knowledge bar that extends to advisers and to matters merely "discoverable". Combined with 2.6 it would make virtually every claim arguable as excluded.
- Playbook: delete entirely. If anything is conceded, it is limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals, mirrored by a Seller knowledge qualifier naming specific Seller persons with a reasonable-enquiry standard, and never applying to Title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### 2.8 Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3) – REJECT, material condition
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.
- Facts (Seller Disclosure Letter para 2): ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30% of revenue); clause 11.2 consent required with **conditions in 11.3**; **no consent exists and no evidence conditions are satisfied**.
- Playbook: effective consent **and** evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion. Consent-on-delivery is insufficient because a conditional consent delivered but unsatisfied gives Bluefen a termination right post-Completion. Reasonable endeavours is too weak for a 30%-revenue customer; we want a hard CP with a Seller obligation to procure.

### 2.9 Riverlark facility (cl 2/7) – REJECT post-completion release
- Seller: release "to be provided following Completion".
- Facts (para 3): ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, change-of-control cl 8.1, discharge cl 9.2, **not repaid, no discharge included**.
- Playbook: current payout letter from Riverlark, direct repayment from Completion funds via the funds flow, and effective security releases (PPSR and any other registrations) delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval; neither exists. Note also that a debt-free/cash-free price mechanic cannot work if AUD 3.2m of debt is left unresolved at Completion.

### 2.10 Funds flow / employee bonuses (DD-005) – REJECT exclusion
- Seller: "agreed price mechanics"; bonuses "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised.
- Facts (para 5): AUD 420,000 of Completion-triggered bonuses, conditional on Completion and continued employment; **not in the funds flow**; on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) not addressed.
- Playbook: these are triggered by our Completion and will be paid by the Company we are buying. They must be a specific funds-flow line item (price deduction or Seller-funded at Completion), **including** payroll tax, superannuation and any other on-costs. "A matter for the Seller" is meaningless unless the Seller actually funds them, and the funds flow currently excludes them silently. We should also reject the "agreed price mechanics" label – nothing in the funds flow is agreed.

### 2.11 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) – BROADEN indemnity
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
- Facts (para 4): DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open (not bank-verified); no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- Playbook: the exposure is not just AUD 180,000 – it is ownership of the Project Materials themselves. Broaden the indemnity to cover loss arising from any failure of the Company to own the SOW3 Project Materials and any Ironquay claim, while preserving the cure route (pay outstanding fees and obtain confirmatory assignment before Completion, ideally as a CP or Completion deliverable). The AUD 180,000 figure should be verified against bank records and Ironquay confirmation; we neither accept nor dispute it.

### 2.12 Export/privacy incident (DD-006, cl 4.6/Sch 6) – DO NOT accept "not material"
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
- Facts (para 6): download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); access, scope and notification duty **undetermined**; investigation preliminary.
- Playbook: we assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss in either direction, and we do not accept the Seller's "not material" conclusion either. Require: preservation of logs; a completed investigation with findings delivered before Completion; ongoing update obligations; a Schedule 6 specific indemnity (uncapped by the general regime) for losses arising from the incident including any notification or regulatory response; and a warranty that the Disclosure is complete and accurate as at Completion.

### 2.13 Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011, AUD 330,000) – ASSESS, no automatic treatment
- Seller: ordinary-course operating costs.
- Facts (para 8): three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each; the Seller does not state whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.
- Playbook: neither accept the "ordinary course" characterisation nor assert an automatic Debt/price deduction. Diligence request: timing, termination rights, whether accrued or prepaid, whether they relate to pre- or post-Completion services. If accrued or committed pre-Completion with post-Completion benefit, address through working capital or a specific adjustment, not Debt by default.

### 2.14 Tax / IP – OPEN, not settled
- Seller: "settled under the general regime".
- Playbook: Tax and IP remain OPEN and are separate categories. We assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. Reject the "settled" characterisation and reserve our position on a Tax Indemnity/Tax Warranty regime with its own cap and claims period, and an IP regime separate from the general cap.

### 2.15 Title evidence (DD-012) – INSUFFICIENT
- Seller: title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012".
- Facts (para 10): the register is a Company-supplied internal document; the Seller confirms it does not reflect Buyer verification.
- Playbook: require independent evidence – ASIC extract and historical member search, PPSR and charge searches against the Company and the Seller, Seller board/shareholder authorities, share certificates or confirmation none issued, and confirmation no options, convertibles, pre-emptive rights or trusts over the shares. This supports, but does not replace, the uncapped Title regime in 2.4.

### 2.16 Lesser points
- **Office lease (DD-007)** – notification only; confirm the notification mechanics and timing, ensure it is a Seller pre-Completion covenant, and verify there is no change-of-control termination right buried in the lease.
- **Mossvale (DD-009)** – restriction on assignment; share sale is not an assignment on the disclosed wording. Confirm there is no separate change-of-control clause; obtain a Seller warranty to that effect.
- **Data-room cut-off** – disclosure is "as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026"; we need bring-down at Completion and a Seller obligation to disclose intervening events (without those disclosures qualifying the Warranties for claim purposes).

## 3. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m.** 20% not authorised – no Amelia Frost approval exists |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k, excess-only | **5k / 50k, first-dollar** |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months | **24 months.** 18 not authorised |
| 4 | "All limitations apply to all Claims" | Proposed | **Delete**; limitations confined to General Warranty Claims |
| 5 | Title/capacity | Same as general | **Separate regime: 100%, ≥6 years, no basket/knowledge bar** |
| 6 | Fraud carve-out | Absent | **Insert**; carved out of everything; non-waivable |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | **Specific fair disclosure only**; delete paras 1.1–1.2 |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket incl. advisers/discoverable | **Delete** |
| 9 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours, consent-on-delivery | **Hard CP: effective consent + evidence 11.3 conditions satisfied** |
| 10 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | **Payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion** |
| 11 | DD-005 bonuses | Not in funds flow | **Specific line item incl. on-costs, or Seller-funded** |
| 12 | Ironquay | SOW3 payment only | **Broaden to ownership of Project Materials; preserve cure; verify AUD 180k** |
| 13 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | **Investigate, preserve logs, updates, specific indemnity; no conclusion either way** |
| 14 | Sandbar | "Ordinary course" | **Assess via diligence; no automatic treatment** |
| 15 | Tax/IP | "Settled" | **OPEN; separate regimes** |
| 16 | Title evidence | DD-012 register | **Independent searches and authorities** |

**Overall assessment:** the Seller draft departs from the playbook on every major limitation point and the gap is wide, not incremental. The combined effect of the cap, deductible basket, 18-month period, whole-data-room disclosure, constructive buyer-knowledge bar, and absence of any fraud carve-out would leave the warranty package largely illusory. On the deal-specific risks (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006), the Seller's cover note overstates progress and its own Disclosure Letter confirms nothing has been resolved. We should respond with a full mark-up at playbook opening positions, and any movement to the 20% cap or 18-month period must first be cleared in writing by Amelia Frost with reference to this Seller draft.

Broaden the indemnity to cover loss arising from any failure of the Company to own the SOW3 Project Materials and any Ironquay claim, while preserving the cure route (pay outstanding fees and obtain confirmatory assignment before Completion, ideally as a CP or Completion deliverable). The AUD 180,000 figure should be verified against bank records and Ironquay confirmation; we neither accept nor dispute it.

### 2.12 Export/privacy incident (DD-006, cl 4.6/Sch 6) – DO NOT accept "not material"
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
- Facts (para 6): download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); access, scope and notification duty **undetermined**; investigation preliminary.
- Playbook: we assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss in either direction, and we do not accept the Seller's "not material" conclusion either. Require: preservation of logs; a completed investigation with findings delivered before Completion; ongoing update obligations; a Schedule 6 specific indemnity (uncapped by the general regime) for losses arising from the incident including any notification or regulatory response; and a warranty that the Disclosure is complete and accurate as at Completion.

### 2.13 Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011, AUD 330,000) – ASSESS, no automatic treatment
- Seller: ordinary-course operating costs.
- Facts (para 8): three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each; the Seller does not state whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.
- Playbook: neither accept the "ordinary course" characterisation nor assert an automatic Debt/price deduction. Diligence request: timing, termination rights, whether accrued or prepaid, whether they relate to pre- or post-Completion services. If accrued or committed pre-Completion with post-Completion benefit, address through working capital or a specific adjustment, not Debt by default.

### 2.14 Tax / IP – OPEN, not settled
- Seller: "settled under the general regime".
- Playbook: Tax and IP remain OPEN and are separate categories. We assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. Reject the "settled" characterisation and reserve our position on a Tax Indemnity/Tax Warranty regime with its own cap and claims period, and an IP regime separate from the general cap.

### 2.15 Title evidence (DD-012) – INSUFFICIENT
- Seller: title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012".
- Facts (para 10): the register is a Company-supplied internal document; the Seller confirms it does not reflect Buyer verification.
- Playbook: require independent evidence – ASIC extract and historical member search, PPSR and charge searches against the Company and the Seller, Seller board/shareholder authorities, share certificates or confirmation none issued, and confirmation no options, convertibles, pre-emptive rights or trusts over the shares. This supports, but does not replace, the uncapped Title regime in 2.4.

### 2.16 Lesser points
- **Office lease (DD-007)** – notification only; confirm the notification mechanics and timing, ensure it is a Seller pre-Completion covenant, and verify there is no change-of-control termination right buried in the lease.
- **Mossvale (DD-009)** – restriction on assignment; share sale is not an assignment on the disclosed wording. Confirm there is no separate change-of-control clause; obtain a Seller warranty to that effect.
- **Data-room cut-off** – disclosure is "as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026"; we need bring-down at Completion and a Seller obligation to disclose intervening events (without those disclosures qualifying the Warranties for claim purposes).
